subject: stat_bin miscalculates ..density.. when bins are very small

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: stat_bin miscalculates ..density.. when bins are very small
parts:
Starting with this histogram:

visited <- structure(list(x = c(7L, 27L, 7L, 74L, 12L, NA, 17L, 10L, 9L,
NA, NA, NA, 15L, 10L, NA, 16L, 19L, 38L, 53L, NA, 16L, 60L, NA,
15L, 18L, NA, 42L, NA, 1L, 53L, 10L, 50L, 6L, 0L, NA, 20L, 4L,
26L, 37L, 1L, 4L, NA, 9L, 23L, 3L, 11L, NA, NA, 31L, NA, 0L,
NA, 5L, 17L, 58L, 3L, 2L, 15L, 10L, NA, NA, 28L, 36L, 0L, 1L,
12L, 9L, 32L, 105L, 8L, NA, NA, 7L, 0L, NA, NA, 0L, NA, NA, 2L,
3L, 14L, 5L, NA, 2L, 1L, NA, NA, 74L, 19L, NA, NA, 6L, NA, 3L,
4L, 3L, NA, NA, 9L, 19L, 1L, 34L, NA, 53L, 3L, NA, NA, 3L, 6L,
NA, 6L, 2L, 38L, NA, 3L, 2L, 17L, 29L, 36L, NA, 7L, 3L, 3L, 5L,
10L, 2L, 10L, NA, 0L, 1L, 1L, 14L, 18L, 15L, 4L, NA, 41L, 26L,
33L, 10L, NA)), .Names = "x", row.names = c(NA, -142L), class = "data.frame")

ggplot2(visited) + geom_histogram(aes(x=x), binwidth=2, right=FALSE)

I'd like to scale *both* axes to be in percent. I can do that for the
y-axis like so:

ggplot2(visited) + geom_histogram(aes(x=x, y=..density..), binwidth=2,
right=FALSE) +
scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent", limits=c(0,.1))

or I can do it for the x-axis like so:

ggplot2(visited) + geom_histogram(aes(x=x/7012), binwidth=2/7012, right=FALSE) +
scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent", limits=c(0,.02))

(the magic number 7012 is the known-from-experimental-design largest
possible entry in the 'x' vector, which nobody came even remotely
close to) But if I try to combine the two, logically this *should*
work...

ggplot2(visited) + geom_histogram(aes(x=x/7012, y=..density..),
binwidth=2/7012, right=FALSE) +
scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent", limits=c(0,.1)) +
scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent", limits=c(0,.02))

but instead gives me a blank graph. Removing the limits on the y-axis
restores the graph, but the percentages are ridiculously enormous --
10,000% to 50,000%. I can only conclude that ..density.. is not
fulfilling its contract to integrate to 1 when the bins are this
narrow.

Any advice? Is there a better way to do this?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a

parts:
> but instead gives me a blank graph.  Removing the limits on the y-axis
> restores the graph, but the percentages are ridiculously enormous --
> 10,000% to 50,000%.  I can only conclude that ..density.. is not
> fulfilling its contract to integrate to 1 when the bins are this
> narrow.

The bin width is 2/7012, which means the total height needs to be 7012
/ 2 to integrate to be one - that seems about right for that graph.

Hadley

Hi Zack -

I was going to write a more instructive email, but as I started working more on your problem, I realized that I really have no idea what you want.  Generally speaking, if you don't like stat_bin (or it's not calculating what you want), just script the stat yourself and use geom_rect to make the plot.  You can do it in a handful of lines, so it's really easy :

counts <- as.numeric(table(cut(visited$x, breaks = (0:11) * 10)))
df <- data.frame(
  xmin = (0:10) * 10,
  xmax = (1:11) * 10,
  ymin = rep(0, 11),
  ymax = counts 
)
ggplot(data = df) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax))

That being said, in most cases the structure of ggplot is there for a reason, especially with something so common as stat_bin, so be careful when you rig your own graphic and strong-arm ggplot into drawing it - you may just be making something that makes no sense or, worse, is misleading.

Hope it helps
david.
